title: Wuthering Heights
descr: Wuthering Heights, Emily Brontë's only novel, was published in 1847 under the pseudonym "Ellis Bell". It was written between October 1845 and June 1846. Wuthering Heights and Anne Brontë's Agnes Grey were accepted by publisher Thomas Newby before the success of their sister Charlotte's novel Jane Eyre. After Emily's death, Charlotte edited the manuscript of Wuthering Heights and arranged for the edited version to be published as a posthumous second edition in 1850.

title: Jane Eyre
descr: Jane Eyre /ɛər/ (originally published as Jane Eyre: An Autobiography) is a novel by English writer Charlotte Brontë, published under the pen name "Currer Bell", on 16 October 1847, by Smith, Elder & Co. of London. The first American edition was published the following year by Harper & Brothers of New York. Primarily a bildungsroman, Jane Eyre follows the experiences of its eponymous heroine, including her growth to adulthood and her love for Mr. Rochester, the brooding master of Thornfield Hall. The novel revolutionised prose fiction in that the focus on Jane's moral and spiritual development is told through an intimate, first-person narrative, where actions and events are coloured by a psychological intensity. The book contains elements of social criticism, with a strong sense of Christian morality at its core and is considered by many to be ahead of its time because of Jane's individualistic character and how the novel approaches the topics of class, sexuality, religion and feminism.

title: The Raven
descr: "The Raven" is a narrative poem by American writer Edgar Allan Poe. First published in January 1845, the poem is often noted for its musicality, stylized language, and supernatural atmosphere. It tells of a talking raven's mysterious visit to a distraught lover, tracing the man's slow fall into madness. The lover, often identified as being a student, is lamenting the loss of his love, Lenore. Sitting on a bust of Pallas, the raven seems to further distress the protagonist with its constant repetition of the word "Nevermore". The poem makes use of folk, mythological, religious, and classical references.

title: Eleonora
descr: "Eleonora" is a short story by Edgar Allan Poe, first published in 1842 in Philadelphia in the literary annual The Gift. It is often regarded as somewhat autobiographical and has a relatively "happy" ending.

title: Catweazle
descr: Catweazle is a British fantasy television series, starring Geoffrey Bayldon in the title role, and created by Richard Carpenter for London Weekend Television. The first series, produced and directed by Quentin Lawrence, was screened in the UK on ITV in 1970. The second series, directed by David Reid and David Lane, was shown in 1971. Each series had thirteen episodes, most but not all written by Carpenter, who also published two books based on the scripts.

title: The Importance of Being Earnest
descr: Oscar Wilde's 1895 comedy of manners satirizes Victorian social conventions through two bachelors, Jack and Algernon, who each adopt the fictitious persona of 'Ernest' to escape obligations, leading to farcical confusion, mistaken identities, and witty epigrams on marriage and respectability.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
descr: Oscar Wilde's only novel (1890) tells of a beautiful young man whose portrait ages and bears the corruption of his sins while he remains outwardly youthful, exploring aestheticism, moral duplicity, and the price of hedonism.

title: Pygmalion
descr: George Bernard Shaw's 1913 play follows phonetics professor Henry Higgins, who wagers he can pass off Cockney flower girl Eliza Doolittle as a duchess by teaching her refined speech, probing class, identity, and transformation.

title: Man and Superman
descr: Shaw's 1903 comedy-drama uses the pursuit of confirmed bachelor Jack Tanner by the determined Ann Whitefield to dramatize the 'Life Force' and Shaw's ideas on marriage, evolution, and the battle of the sexes, including the 'Don Juan in Hell' dream sequence.

title: A Dolls House
descr: Henrik Ibsen's 1879 drama depicts Nora Helmer, who abandons her comfortable but stifling marriage after realizing she has been treated as a doll, a landmark in modern theatre for its critique of 19th-century gender roles.

title: Ghosts
descr: Ibsen's 1881 tragedy confronts inherited disease, hypocrisy, and duty as Mrs. Alving's carefully preserved image of her late husband collapses and her son Oswald succumbs to the consequences of the past.

title: The Cherry Orchard
descr: Anton Chekhov's final play (1904) portrays an aristocratic Russian family unable to prevent the sale of their beloved estate and cherry orchard, capturing social change and the fading of the old order with tragicomic subtlety.

title: Uncle Vanya
descr: Chekhov's 1898 play examines disillusionment and wasted lives on a rural estate, as Vanya confronts the emptiness of his sacrifices for a pompous retired professor, blending melancholy and quiet humour.

title: Three Sisters
descr: Chekhov's 1901 drama follows the Prozorov sisters—Olga, Masha, and Irina—longing to return to Moscow while provincial life erodes their hopes, a study of yearning, stagnation, and the passage of time.

title: Oedipus Rex
descr: Sophocles' tragedy (c. 429 BCE) dramatizes King Oedipus's relentless search for the murderer of Laius, only to discover he himself unknowingly killed his father and married his mother, a cornerstone of dramatic irony and fate.

title: Antigone
descr: Sophocles' tragedy (c. 441 BCE) depicts Antigone defying King Creon's edict to bury her brother, dramatizing the conflict between divine law and civic authority, conscience and power.

title: Medea
descr: Euripides' tragedy (431 BCE) portrays Medea's ferocious revenge on her unfaithful husband Jason, culminating in the killing of their children, a searing exploration of passion, betrayal, and the position of women.

title: The Bacchae
descr: Euripides' late tragedy (c. 405 BCE) shows the god Dionysus bringing his ecstatic cult to Thebes and destroying King Pentheus, who resists him, dramatizing the dangers of denying irrational, divine forces.

title: Prometheus Bound
descr: Attributed to Aeschylus, this tragedy depicts the Titan Prometheus, chained to a rock as punishment by Zeus for giving fire to humankind, defiantly enduring his torment—an emblem of rebellion against tyranny.

title: The Oresteia
descr: Aeschylus's trilogy (458 BCE) traces the cycle of vengeance in the house of Atreus—from Agamemnon's murder to Orestes' matricide and trial—culminating in the establishment of justice and civic law.

title: Death of a Salesman
descr: Arthur Miller's 1949 Pulitzer-winning tragedy follows aging salesman Willy Loman as his illusions of success collapse, a piercing critique of the American Dream and its toll on the ordinary man.

title: The Crucible
descr: Miller's 1953 drama dramatizes the Salem witch trials as an allegory for McCarthy-era hysteria, portraying how fear, rumor, and rigid authority destroy a community.

title: A Streetcar Named Desire
descr: Tennessee Williams's 1947 Pulitzer-winning play sets the fragile, fading Blanche DuBois against her brutish brother-in-law Stanley Kowalski in New Orleans, exploring desire, illusion, and cruelty.

title: The Glass Menagerie
descr: Williams's 1944 'memory play' portrays the Wingfield family—overbearing Amanda, fragile Laura with her glass figurines, and restless Tom—yearning to escape their confined lives.

title: Waiting for Godot
descr: Samuel Beckett's 1953 tragicomedy presents two tramps, Vladimir and Estragon, waiting endlessly for the mysterious Godot who never arrives, a defining work of the Theatre of the Absurd.

title: Endgame
descr: Beckett's 1957 one-act play confines blind, immobile Hamm and his servant Clov in a bare room at the world's end, distilling dependence, futility, and the endgame of existence.

title: The Ballad of Reading Gaol
descr: Oscar Wilde's 1898 poem, written after his imprisonment, reflects on a fellow inmate's execution and the shared guilt and suffering of prisoners, condemning the brutality of the penal system.

title: Lady Windermeres Fan
descr: Wilde's 1892 society comedy turns on a fan, a misunderstanding, and a woman with a secret past, satirizing rigid Victorian morality and the double standard of reputation.

title: An Ideal Husband
descr: Wilde's 1895 comedy exposes political and personal hypocrisy as a public man's hidden misdeed threatens his marriage and career, balancing wit with a plea for compassion and forgiveness.

title: Arms and the Man
descr: Shaw's 1894 comedy undercuts romantic ideals of war and heroism through the pragmatic 'chocolate cream soldier' Bluntschli, who upends a Bulgarian family's illusions of glory and love.

title: Candida
descr: Shaw's 1894 domestic comedy centers on the poised Candida choosing between her clergyman husband and a lovestruck young poet, wryly reversing conventional expectations of strength and dependence.

title: Saint Joan
descr: Shaw's 1923 historical drama depicts Joan of Arc's visions, victories, trial, and execution, portraying her as a proto-Protestant and nationalist heroine caught between church and state.

title: The Wild Duck
descr: Ibsen's 1884 tragicomedy shows how the meddling idealist Gregers Werle, insisting on absolute truth, shatters the comforting illusions that sustain the Ekdal family, with devastating results.

title: Rosmersholm
descr: Ibsen's 1886 drama traces former pastor Rosmer and Rebecca West as guilt, radical ideals, and a haunting past drive them toward a shared tragic end at Rosmersholm.

title: The Master Builder
descr: Ibsen's 1892 play follows the aging architect Halvard Solness, fearful of youth supplanting him, whose fateful attraction to the young Hilde Wangel leads to his symbolic, fatal ascent.

title: The Seagull
descr: Chekhov's 1896 play interweaves unrequited loves and artistic ambition around a lakeside estate, as aspiring writer Konstantin and actress Nina clash with the established generation, blending comedy and tragedy.

title: Ivanov
descr: Chekhov's 1887 play portrays the disillusioned, debt-ridden Ivanov spiraling into despair and self-destruction, an early study of the aimless, melancholic anti-hero.

title: The Wood Demon
descr: An early Chekhov play (1889) and precursor to Uncle Vanya, exploring provincial estate life, unhappy relationships, and disillusionment among the landed gentry.

title: Electra
descr: Sophocles' tragedy dramatizes Electra's grief and thirst for vengeance as she and her brother Orestes plot to kill their mother Clytemnestra and Aegisthus to avenge their father Agamemnon.

title: Ajax
descr: Sophocles' tragedy depicts the great warrior Ajax, maddened by the loss of Achilles' armor to Odysseus, whose shame at his humiliation drives him to suicide, and the debate over his burial.

title: Philoctetes
descr: Sophocles' tragedy (409 BCE) portrays the abandoned, wounded archer Philoctetes on Lemnos, and the moral conflict of Neoptolemus torn between deceit and honor in retrieving him for the Trojan War.

title: The Trojan Women
descr: Euripides' tragedy (415 BCE) presents the enslaved women of fallen Troy—Hecuba, Cassandra, Andromache—as they mourn their dead and face captivity, a powerful anti-war lament.

title: Electra
descr: Euripides' tragedy retells the vengeance of Electra and Orestes on their mother Clytemnestra, notably placing Electra in humble, rustic circumstances and questioning the justice of matricide.

title: Ion
descr: Euripides' tragicomedy dramatizes the reunion of Ion, a temple servant at Delphi, with his mother Creusa, exploring divine paternity, identity, and the ambiguous workings of the gods.

title: Agamemnon
descr: The first play of Aeschylus's Oresteia (458 BCE): King Agamemnon returns victorious from Troy only to be murdered by his wife Clytemnestra, setting the cycle of vengeance in motion.

title: The Libation Bearers
descr: The second play of the Oresteia: Orestes returns to avenge his father by killing his mother Clytemnestra and Aegisthus, guided by Apollo and reunited with his sister Electra at Agamemnon's tomb.

title: The Eumenides
descr: The final play of the Oresteia: the Furies pursue Orestes for matricide until Athena establishes a court in Athens, transforming blood vengeance into civic justice.

title: All My Sons
descr: Miller's 1947 drama exposes wartime profiteering as the Keller family confronts the truth that faulty aircraft parts, knowingly shipped, caused pilots' deaths, weighing private gain against public responsibility.

title: A View from the Bridge
descr: Miller's 1955 tragedy set among Brooklyn dockworkers follows longshoreman Eddie Carbone, whose possessive love for his niece and betrayal of illegal immigrants lead to his downfall.

title: The Price
descr: Miller's 1968 play reunites two estranged brothers to sell their late father's furniture, forcing a reckoning with old resentments, sacrifice, and the choices that shaped their lives.

title: The Night of the Iguana
descr: Williams's 1961 drama strands a defrocked minister-turned-tour-guide at a Mexican hotel among desperate souls, dramatizing spiritual crisis, endurance, and fragile human connection.

title: Sweet Bird of Youth
descr: Williams's 1959 play follows fading actress Alexandra del Lago and ambitious gigolo Chance Wayne in a decaying Southern town, exploring lost youth, corruption, and vanished dreams.

title: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
descr: Williams's 1955 Pulitzer-winning drama confronts a wealthy Southern family with mendacity, greed, and repressed desire during Big Daddy's birthday, as Maggie and Brick's troubled marriage unravels.

title: Krapp Last Tape
descr: Beckett's 1958 one-act monologue features an old man listening to and recording tapes of his younger self, meditating on memory, regret, and lost love.

title: Happy Days
descr: Beckett's 1961 play shows the relentlessly cheerful Winnie, buried to her waist and then her neck in earth, chattering to fill the void—an image of endurance amid absurdity.

title: Play
descr: Beckett's 1963 short play confines three figures in funeral urns who compulsively recount a love triangle in rapid, spotlight-triggered speech, dissecting repetition and purgatorial guilt.

title: Villette
descr: Charlotte Brontë's 1853 novel follows the reserved Lucy Snowe teaching at a boarding school in the fictional town of Villette, a subtle, psychologically intense study of isolation, longing, and repression.

title: The Professor
descr: Charlotte Brontë's first-written novel (published posthumously 1857) narrates William Crimsworth's career and courtship in Brussels, drawing on Brontë's own Continental experiences.

title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall
descr: Anne Brontë's 1848 novel, framed as letters and a diary, recounts the mysterious Helen Graham's flight from an abusive, dissolute husband, a bold early feminist critique of marriage.

title: Politian
descr: Edgar Allan Poe's only play, an unfinished verse tragedy (1835) set in Renaissance Rome, dramatizing love, betrayal, and revenge in Poe's characteristically dark Romantic style.

title: The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym
descr: Poe's only complete novel (1838) recounts young Pym's harrowing sea voyage of mutiny, shipwreck, cannibalism, and eerie Antarctic mystery, a pioneering work of adventure and the uncanny.

title: The Fall of the House of Usher
descr: Poe's 1839 Gothic tale follows a visitor to the decaying Usher mansion, where the doomed siblings Roderick and Madeline embody dread, madness, and the collapse of an ancient house.

title: The Masque of the Red Death
descr: Poe's 1842 allegorical tale depicts Prince Prospero's masquerade, sealed against a deadly plague, where the personified Red Death nonetheless claims all—an emblem of inescapable mortality.

title: The Cask of Amontillado
descr: Poe's 1846 tale of chilling revenge is narrated by Montresor, who lures the wine connoisseur Fortunato into catacombs and walls him up alive, a masterpiece of the unreliable narrator.

title: Ligeia
descr: Poe's 1838 Gothic tale of obsession and death recounts the narrator's love for the intellectual Ligeia and her uncanny return, exploring will, identity, and the boundary between life and death.
